title: AI-based Estimation of the Diastolic Pressure Ratio (DPR) in Proximal LAD Stenoses Compared with Invasively Measured DPR: A Retrospective Analysis Using Commercial AI Systems (PROX-LAD-DPR Study)
summary: In some cardiac catheterization procedures, a thin wire is used to measure how strongly a narrowing in a heart artery restricts blood flow. This measurement is time-consuming and carries small risks. We ask whether computer programs using artificial intelligence can estimate this value from the X-ray images of the procedure alone, and which program is the most accurate. For this, we analyze data from earlier examinations at Klinikum Oberberg. The images are anonymized beforehand so that no individual can be identified. We compare the programs' estimates with the values actually measured. No new examinations are performed.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of routine clinical data. Consecutive patients with a 40–80% proximal LAD stenosis and an invasive DPR measurement obtained in clinical routine are included. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Stable coronary artery disease or non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome; angiographically confirmed 40–80% stenosis of the proximal LAD; invasive DPR measurement by pressure wire performed in clinical routine; evaluable digital coronary angiography images (at least two projections showing the target LAD stenosis).
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or non-evaluable angiography data; acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction; prior bypass surgery or stent implantation in the territory of the target LAD; known objection by the patient to the use of their data for research.
